lessons.title: Sexual propagation: growing plants from seed
lessons.html:
What is propagation?

Propagation means producing new plants. There are two main ways: sexual propagation from seed, and vegetative (asexual) propagation from parts of a parent plant.

How seed forms

Seed forms when pollen from the male part of a flower fertilises the female part. Because two parents are involved, seedlings can differ from each other and from the parent. Hybrid seed (F1) is produced by crossing selected parents; it gives uniform, vigorous plants, but seed saved from hybrids does not grow true to type.

What a seed needs to germinate

  • Water: the seed absorbs water and swells.
  • Oxygen: waterlogged media suffocate seeds.
  • Suitable temperature: e.g. warm-season crops like tomatoes, peppers and pumpkins need warm soil; cool-season crops like cabbage and lettuce germinate in cooler conditions.
  • Light or darkness: some small seeds such as lettuce need light; others germinate in darkness.

Seed quality

Buy certified seed from reputable suppliers. Check the packet for cultivar, germination percentage, test date and any seed treatment. Treated seed is coated with a pesticide: handle it with gloves, never use it as food or feed, and follow the label.

Sowing methods

  • Direct sowing in the field: maize, wheat, beans, carrots.
  • Seedling trays in a nursery, then transplanting: tomatoes, cabbages, peppers, onions.

Advantages and disadvantages

AdvantagesDisadvantages
Cheap and easy for large areasPlants may vary (except hybrids)
Seed stores wellSome trees take years to bear fruit from seed
Few diseases pass through seedSome seeds have dormancy and germinate poorly

Dormancy can be broken by soaking, scarifying (nicking the hard coat) or cold treatment, depending on the species.

lessons.title: Vegetative propagation methods
lessons.html:
Plants from plant parts

Vegetative propagation uses a stem, leaf, root or bud from one parent. The new plant is a genetic copy (clone), so it keeps the exact qualities of the parent, such as fruit taste or flower colour.

Main methods

MethodHow it worksExamples
CuttingsA piece of stem, leaf or root is planted and forms roots, often helped by rooting hormone.Sweet potato, grapevine, many ornamentals, herbs
GraftingA scion (shoot of the fruiting cultivar) is joined onto a rootstock.Citrus, avocado, apples, mangoes
BuddingA single bud is inserted into a rootstock.Citrus, roses, stone fruit
LayeringA stem roots while still attached to the parent.Some shrubs, strawberries via runners
DivisionA clump is split into parts with roots and shoots.Agapanthus, grasses, herbs
Bulbs, tubers, cormsStorage organs are planted.Potatoes, onions, garlic
Tissue cultureTiny pieces grow in sterile lab conditions.Bananas, sugarcane, some berries

Why use rootstocks?

Rootstocks can give tolerance to soil diseases, drought or salinity and control tree size, while the scion gives fruit quality.

Hygiene in propagation

  • Take material only from healthy, true-to-type, preferably certified mother plants.
  • Use clean, sharp knives and disinfect them between plants to avoid spreading viruses.
  • Use clean trays and sterile media.

Safety

Grafting knives are very sharp: cut away from your body and keep fingers behind the blade. Wear gloves with rooting hormones and disinfectants and follow the label.

Choosing a method

Consider the crop, cost, speed, the need for true-to-type plants and disease risk.

Key points

  • Sexual propagation uses seed; vegetative propagation uses plant parts.
  • Seed needs water, oxygen and the right temperature to germinate.
  • Vegetative methods produce clones that keep parent qualities.
  • Grafting joins a scion to a rootstock for quality plus root benefits.
  • Clean tools and healthy mother plants prevent spreading disease.
